topics.topic: A02 validation rules inherited by binding ports
questions: Must every binding port schema pass the same supported-subset validation as a contract port, and at what point in rule 5 is that checked?
Must binding port schemas also be within the supported JSON Schema subset, or are the two expressly named A02 port rules the only A02 rules inherited here?
Exactly which A02 port rules apply to binding ports, including schema-subset, cardinality and disclosure-class rules?

judgement.why: P20 judged the same supported-schema question on unchanged later-state text.

precedent.topic: Supported-schema enforcement for non-contract ports and constants
quotes:
a
   schema is a JSON object using only `type` (one of `null`, `boolean`,
   `integer`, `number`, `string`, `array`, `object`, as one string), `enum`
   (a non-empty array of distinct scalars), `const` (one scalar), `properties`
   and `required` (for `object`), `additionalProperties` (`true` or `false`
   only), `items` (one schema, for `array`), `minItems`, `maxItems`,
   `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minimum` and `maximum`. Any other keyword —
   `$ref`, `pattern`, `format`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `not` among them —
   is outside the subset: A02 refuses it in a contract version, and
   `fit_port_value` answers that no value fits it, so a binding or flow port
   written outside the subset can never deliver.

A flow constant is a typed literal
   (M16): the composing agent declares its `value_schema` with its class, and its
   StoredValue takes both. Composition refuses a constant whose value does not
   fit its declared schema (A05 rule 7); phase 2 of the proof checks that the
   declared schema is the target port's stored schema (M21), so the value then
   fits the port (A05 rule 1); the constant's identity does not depend on
   resolving another record.
precedent.why: State 6 defines the supported subset, makes unsupported binding or flow-port schemas accept no value, and therefore makes a constant under such a schema fail composition's value-fit check.

topics.topic: Authoritative required category set for security-review completeness
questions: Against what closed category list can the security gate verify that the review is complete rather than merely verifying the categories that happen to be present?

What authoritative closed set determines the required security categories, so that omitted categories can be detected rather than the review being complete merely because every category it happens to list has an outcome?
What closed list or deterministic procedure decides which security-review categories are required, so the completeness claim can be checked without trusting the review itself?

quotes:
The review covers every actor and boundary accepted in State 0: the owner and the
agents on the one `mcp` channel behind the host's reverse proxy, agent-written
code, the microservices the kernel calls over their HTTP APIs, the platform
manifest, and the host that holds the installation. Each category below was
determined from those boundaries.

state2_security_gate_pass
<-> every_required_category_has_one_outcome
    AND every_APPLICABLE_references_an_accepted_decision
    AND no_UNRESOLVED
`design_lint --state 2` accepts exactly one complete review record.
judgement.divergence: One gate treats the nine categories printed in A21 as the closed required set, while another derives or imports a broader checklist and rejects omitted categories; the owner and design generator notice different State 2 pass/fail results.
judgement.why: The texts require completeness but define neither a closed category set nor a deterministic derivation procedure.

topics.topic: Bounded handling and failure behavior of sandbox stdout and stderr
questions: How are stdout and stderr drained and bounded, and what outcome results when code writes without limit?
Where do stdout and stderr go, and what prevents unbounded printing from blocking the child or consuming unbounded parent memory or storage?

quotes: execute_function: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] The sandboxed process's standard input, standard output and standard error MUST be connected to /dev/null, so nothing the code prints is read, kept, counted toward output_bytes or able to fill a pipe or the scratch area; code that writes without end is stopped only by its wall deadline and concludes timeout; the exception type and message reach the parent through the exchange channel, never through standard error (A03 rules 5 and 6).
judgement.why: The later sandbox contract connects all three standard streams to `/dev/null` and classifies endless writing by the wall deadline as `timeout`.

topics.topic: Exact pinned dependency and sandbox-runtime set for release v1
questions: What exact dependency set, CPython patch/build, bubblewrap version, and other sandbox-runtime artifacts constitute release v1?
Which dependencies exist, and which exact versions—including `bubblewrap` if it is part of the sandbox runtime—does release v1 pin?
Is bubblewrap part of the pinned release dependency set, and if so what exact version or compatibility identity must startup verify?

quotes:
A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of
the sandbox runtime (A03); the sandbox interpreter of release v1 is CPython
3.12, whose `random` module gives A03 rule 4 its list. A vulnerable dependency is answered by a new
release; a running kernel never updates one.

The kernel checks at start, before recovery and before the surface opens,
that `bubblewrap` is present and that one probe execution succeeds; without
both it does not start, and says why. A running kernel therefore always has
a sandbox.
judgement.divergence: Two release builders can choose different dependency sets, CPython patch builds and bubblewrap versions while both claim release v1 compliance; the owner and agents notice differing sandbox behavior, compatibility and vulnerability exposure.
judgement.why: The texts require exact release pins and place them in a release artifact, but never state the artifact's dependency identities or versions.

   no permission for group or others; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.

Before evaluating each request the kernel reads the configuration file and
   compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read; when they differ,
   or the file cannot be read, it re-reads it (K-15) and takes from it only the
   token list. Exactly four checks apply to a re-read: the
   file can be read and parsed; every token is at least 43 characters; no two
   tokens are equal; no two agent tokens share a name (M28). When all four
   hold, the new list replaces the old one.

read_configuration: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check, in this order: config_path is not a regular file or is a symbolic link (checked without following links), is not owned by the process's effective user, or grants any permission to group or others; the bytes cannot be read or do not parse as one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types; a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials; a credential header name is not an HTTP field-name token (one or more of the token characters of RFC 9110: letters, digits and the symbols allowed there); a credential's secret_file is not an absolute path; the owner token or any agent token is shorter than the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant; two tokens among the owner token and the agent tokens are equal; two agent tokens have the same name.

current_token_list: [BEHAVIOR] On every call MUST read the configuration file's bytes and compare their SHA-256 with the last read digest; when equal it returns the kept list unchanged (none stays none); when different, or when the file cannot be read, it re-reads the file and applies exactly four checks: the file can be read and parses as a JSON object with owner_token and agent_tokens of the Installation types, every token is at least the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant long, no two tokens are equal, and no two agent tokens have the same name; the new digest becomes the last read digest, and when the file cannot be read the last read digest is cleared, so the next readable bytes are always re-read.
judgement.divergence: One implementation opens and validates the same descriptor without following links and revalidates ownership and permissions on every reread, while another performs those protections only at startup and later reads by path; a host attacker and the authenticated principals notice whether a substituted token file is accepted.
judgement.why: The later text closes startup no-follow behavior and limits reread validation to four checks, but does not define race-free path resolution or how substitution through a symlinked parent is prevented.
judgement.failure: the quoted passage of a consequential gap is not found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Reliable detection of sandbox resource-limit exhaustion
questions: What observable event proves that memory, process, or scratch limits were hit when user code catches the resulting error and returns valid output?
What observable evidence conclusively classifies a terminated sandbox as resource_exhausted rather than crashed?

quotes: execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] process_count bounds the tasks of the code alive at once: the runner's main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process the code forked with os.fork counts with its threads, and bubblewrap's own processes are not counted, so process_count 1 allows code without threads or forks. Process creation other than os.fork — subprocess, os.system, os.posix_spawn, os.posix_spawnp and the os.exec family — is subprocess use and raises in the audit hook as a trap hit (A03 rule 4). The runner's audit hook, on os.fork and on starting a thread, counts the tasks of the environment's proc and, when the new task would exceed process_count, writes a resource hit to the channel and raises, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error; the parent's setrlimit, set above process_count by the tasks the runner and bubblewrap need, stays the outer bound, and a creation it refuses is reported the same way (A03 required test 2).

execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] A memory, scratch or output bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it from outside: the environment was killed for it, or a MemoryError, or an OSError for a full or over-limit exchange directory, escaped run and reached the parent through the exchange channel; code that catches such an error and returns is judged by what it returned, like any other output (owner, 2026-10-06). Only the process bound is also seen inside, because every thread start and os.fork passes the runner's audit hook.

execute_function: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The outcome is the first that holds, in this order of = models.SandboxOutcome: timeout when the wall deadline passed; resource_exhausted when the memory, process, scratch or output bound was hit; sandbox_violation when the channel recorded any trap hit, even if the code caught it and returned a conforming dict; crashed when the module failed to load, has no run, raised, or the process exited abnormally; contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, a value output cannot be serialized to canonical JSON, a file output is not bytes, a many output is not a list, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded. The stored value ceiling and the spool ceilings are not the sandbox's: the module that stores or spools an output applies them after the execution has otherwise succeeded.
judgement.why: The later sandbox contract defines parent-visible resource evidence, special process-limit reporting, caught-error behavior and the precedence against `crashed`.

topics.topic: Unambiguous run reference to the exact repeated FlowActivation
questions: How does a run unambiguously retain the exact FlowActivation record when the same version may have multiple activation records?
Which activation is recorded when the same flow version was activated, replaced, and activated again before or during the run?
Where is the exact FlowActivation identity for a run stored or deterministically recoverable, especially after the same version is activated again?

quotes:
**Which FlowActivation a `draft-write` send names** (A10 rule 6): the latest
   FlowActivation of the run's pinned version before the Run record in store
   order — the one under which it started. `runs` finds it and passes it to
   `effects` with every call about one of the run's elements (State 3, "Facts
   passed down"); store order, not time, so two records never tie. A run's
   version was active when it started (A12 rule 1), so "none" cannot occur;
   if it does, the store is inconsistent and the call is `internal_error`.

advance_run: [BEHAVIOR] A function element is executed with execute_function_element; an operation element is reached with reach_operation_element, given a RunContext of the run_id, the pinned flow_version_id and started_under the store_position of the FlowActivation read with ActivationBeforeRun, whose absence is raised as StoreInternalError; operation elements that wait are not reached again here.
judgement.why: The later texts recover the exact activation as the latest activation of the pinned version preceding the Run record and pass its store position in the run context.
